Distributions by group: ridgelines, distribution functions, violins, hexagonal bins and concentration curves

Source: R/plotx.R
plotrdg.Rd

Plots of many values, split by a group. plotrdg() stacks a kernel density per group (a ridgeline plot); plotcdfs() overlays the empirical distribution functions; plotvln() draws a violin per group with its median and quartiles; plothex() counts two variables in hexagonal bins, shaded by count; plotgain() overlays the concentration (Lorenz) curves of the groups with their Gini coefficients.

Usage

plotrdg(x, grp = NULL, bw = "nrd0", ..., main = NULL, col = NULL, pal = NULL)

plotcdfs(x, grp = NULL, ..., main = NULL, col = NULL, pal = NULL)

plotvln(x, grp = NULL, bw = "nrd0", ..., main = NULL, col = NULL, pal = NULL)

plothex(x, y, bins = 30L, ..., main = NULL, col = NULL, pal = NULL)

plotgain(x, grp = NULL, ..., main = NULL, col = NULL, pal = NULL)

Arguments

x

Numbers (non-negative for plotgain()).

grp

NULL (one group) or a group per value of x.

bw

The kernel bandwidth: one positive number or a rule known to stats::density() ("nrd0", "nrd", "ucv", "bcv", "sj", "sj-ste", "sj-dpi").

...

Passed to the base-graphics call that draws the frame.

main

NULL (a default title) or one string.

col

NULL (the palette) or colours.

pal

NULL (the session palette, see plotopt()) or a palette name for blpal().

y

For plothex(), numbers, one per value of x.

bins

The number of hexagons across: one whole number from 2 to 500.

Value

Invisibly, a data frame of what was drawn: grp, x and y (the density, or the share at or below), for plotvln() with the quartiles as attribute summary; for plothex() the hexagon centres x, y and count, by row of hexagons and then column; for plotgain() grp, pop and share, with the Gini per group as attribute gini. Values that are not finite are left out.

Examples

set.seed(1)
x <- c(rnorm(100), rnorm(100, 2))
g <- rep(c("a", "b"), each = 100)
plotrdg(x, g)

plotcdfs(x, g)

plotvln(x, g)

plothex(x, x + rnorm(200), bins = 10)

plotgain(rexp(200), g)
